sonnet.problem: The right answer "Drag them away like sheep to slaughter" is the verse's own wording, while the two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing. The right answer sounds more like the Bible than the others and stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

sonnet.problem: The card says "an answer comes to Jeremiah." Jeremiah 12:5 does not say it answers his complaint or who it is spoken to. The card also changes "have said" to "have been saying."
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The question turns the conditional "If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out" into a stated fact: "men on foot have worn Jeremiah out." It also makes "you" Jeremiah, which the text does not say.
